deities: Sree Dharma Sastha / Lord Ayyappan (Harihara Puthiran)

history.dynasty: Tradition: installed by Parasurama; associated with the Pandalam royal family; administered by the Travancore Devaswom Board
history.period: Site of great antiquity; shrine dated to about the 11th century (verify); present structures include a 1950 rebuild
history.summary: Sabarimala Sree Dharma Sastha Temple, atop the Sabarimala hill at 1,260 m in the Western Ghats (Periyar Tiger Reserve), is one of the world's largest annual pilgrimage sites (Wikipedia: 10-15 million devotees yearly - CONFLICT (verify): some travel sites claim 40-50 million). Ayyappa (Ayyappan), son of Shiva and Mohini (Vishnu's female form), is worshipped as a celibate deity; pilgrims observe a 41-day vratham (austerities, abstaining from meat and carnal pleasures) and carry the Irumudi kettu offering bundle. Tradition credits Parasurama with installing the idol; 'Sabarimala' is the mountain of Sabari of the Ramayana. The temple famously admits all castes and creeds - Vavar, a Muslim saint-friend of Ayyappa, is a sub-deity - but restricts entry of women of menstruating age (10-50) by tradition; the 2018 Supreme Court verdict permitting entry remains contested and the restriction is still enforced in practice - CONFLICT (verify current status). The temple opens only during the Mandala-Makaravilakku season (mid-November to mid-January), the first five days of each Malayalam month, Vishu, Onam and Prathishta Dinam.

name: Sabarimala Sree Ayyappa Temple
town_description: CORRECTED: Sabarimala is the hill shrine, not a town; Pamba is its base town. Pamba is a small riverside settlement on the Pampa river in Pathanamthitta district, serving as the base camp for the Sabarimala pilgrimage. It hosts Travancore Devaswom Board facilities - bus stands, annadanam halls, cloak rooms and medical aid - and fills with pilgrims during the Mandala season. From Pamba a 4-5 km forest trek (with the 18 holy steps at the end) leads up to the Sannidhanam.
tradition: Hinduism (Sastha worship; amalgam of Shaiva, Vaishnava and folk traditions)

travel.airport: Cochin International Airport, about 155 km; Thiruvananthapuram Airport about 170 km (verify)
travel.railway: Chengannur railway station, about 90 km; Kottayam about 95 km (verify)
travel.road: Road to Pamba base camp via Nilackal; KSRTC buses ply during season; final 4-5 km ascent is on foot only

visitor_information.best_time: Mandala-Makaravilakku season (mid-November to mid-January); monthly first-five-days darshan is less crowded
visitor_information.opening_hours: Temple opens ONLY during season days (Mandala-Makaravilakku), first five days of each Malayalam month, Vishu, Onam, Prathishta Dinam; daily darshan hours during open periods typically about 3:00 AM-1:00 PM and 4:00-11:00 PM (verify); closed the rest of the year
